title: Runway slot orchestrator: adaptive memory compaction and GPU smoothing for mixed-turn workloads
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response length traffic (short queries interleaved with long generation turns) is causing split failures in our KV residency logic and uneven GPU slab utilization. Symptoms observed in production: elevated p95/p99 tail latency during microbursts, increased GPU memory fragmentation over long runs, occasional OOMs on high-concurrency hosts, and suboptimal throughput due to conservative admission heuristics.

Goal: Build a scheduler-level "Runway Slot Orchestrator" that tunes continuous-batcher admission, adaptive KV residency, and background compaction/defragmentation to improve tail latency and decrease memory churn while preserving throughput. The approach emphasizes soft compaction windows, probabilistic eviction based on token-density, and cooperative CPU spillover for cold long KV sequences.

Why different from prior work: Existing tickets focused on length-prioritized slots, reservoir prefetch, and slot coalescing. This work emphasizes a runway-inspired tenure model (slot runway = short-lived fast-path vs runway-extended slots for long turns) combined with opportunistic compaction/defrag cycles scheduled to low-util intervals and lightweight probabilistic admission to avoid sharp throughput cliffs. The goal is to reduce reactive OOM events and avoid large-scale KV churn that hurts latency.
acceptance_criteria: p95 tail latency for mixed-turn synthetic workload reduced by >= 15% compared to baseline continuous-batcher config
Number of OOM events on canary hosts drops to zero over 48h stress test
GPU memory fragmentation metric (slab_free_ratio variance) reduced by >= 30% measured over a 6h run
No regression in steady-state throughput (within +/- 5%) on dedicated-capacity profiles
Config knobs documented and available behind runtime feature flag (runway_orchestrator=true)
design_notes:
Core concepts: runway-tenure, soft compaction, token-density score, ephemeral KV shard tiers.

1) Runway-tenure: classify incoming requests into three tenure classes: sprint (short turns, aggressive coalescing), cruise (medium, default), runway-extended (long turns, reserved KV residency). Tenure computed from prompt token distribution + request hint + rolling client history.

2) Probabilistic admission: instead of deterministic admit/deny, compute admission probability p = sigmoid(alpha*(token_density - threshold)). This smooths admission under bursts and avoids sudden capacity cliffs.

3) Soft compaction windows: schedule lightweight compaction (KV trimming, merging small slabs) during predicted low-util windows; allow cancel/resume if unexpected burst arrives.

4) Cooperative CPU spillover: long cold sequences are candidates for migration to pinned CPU-backed cache to free GPU slab for active short-turns. Use async prefetch back to GPU before expected next token horizon.

5) Defragmentation heuristic: trigger full slab defrag only when slab_free_ratio < defrag_threshold AND predicted idle > defrag_duration_estimate. Otherwise use micro-trims.

Data-driven parameters documented in spec. Tunables exposed: runway_tenure_thresholds, token_density_alpha, soft_compaction_window_ms, cpu_spill_min_len, defrag_threshold, p_admission_floor.
implementation_notes:
Code touches: scheduler/orchestrator.cc, kv/residency_manager.cc, gpu/slab_allocator.cc, runtime/configs.yaml.

Feature flag: runtime.flags.runway_orchestrator (off by default).

New metrics to emit: runway.tenure_assignment{tenure=sprint|cruise|extended}, runway.admit_prob, runway.evictions_soft, kv.spill_cpu_count, gpu.slab_free_ratio_sampled, runway.compaction_runs{type=micro|full}, runway.defrag_trigger_reason.

API changes: none user-facing. Internal logs for debugging: RUNWAY_ASSIGN, RUNWAY_COMPACT_START/END, KV_SPILL_PUSH/PULL.

Testing harness: extend continuous_batcher_sim with mixed-turn generator (configurable short/long ratio, microburst frequency). Add a deterministic seed mode.

Implementation plan: experimental branch -> lab stress runs -> small canary pool (10 hosts) -> 50% canary -> full rollout with 24h safety window.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for tenure classification and admission probability function.
2) Integration in lab: run continuous_batcher_sim mixed-turn workload against baseline and runway variant for 6h runs; collect metrics and traces.
3) Fault injection: force unexpected microbursts and verify compaction cancellations and no OOMs.
4) Canary: rollout to 10 inference hosts for 48h under production-like traffic, monitor metrics and error budgets.
5) Scale canary to 50% traffic if stable, then full.

Synthetic workload parameters are checked into repo (tests/fixtures/runway_mixed_turns.yaml).
rollout_plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime.flags.runway_orchestrator.
- Stage 1: lab experiments and test harness (complete).
- Stage 2: canary pool (N=10 hosts) for 48h with detailed tracing. Abort if OOM or p95 regress > 10% for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Stage 3: 50% traffic for 24h. Monitor compaction runs and CPU spill rate.
- Stage 4: full rollout.
- Rollback plan: set feature flag off and restart scheduler processes. Quick patch available to revert admitted policy to baseline admission heuristics.
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Spike experiments in lab: implemented tenure classifier prototype and gathered token distribution histograms from sliced production traces (sampled). Observed ~18% of requests qualify as runway-extended under default thresholds.
2026-03-05: Implemented probabilistic admission function and added unit tests. Local sim showed smoother admission curves under synthetic microbursts vs binary admission (reduced reject storms).

2026-03-07: First end-to-end lab run (6h) with mixed-turn generator. Results: p95 down 12%, slab_free_ratio variance down 25%, but cpu_spill_count high during one long-run cluster—tuning needed for cpu_spill_min_len.

2026-03-10: Addressed spill tuning: increased cpu_spill_min_len threshold and added prefetch cooldown. Re-ran stress tests; cpu spills dropped ~60% and p95 improved to 16% vs baseline. Prepared canary config.
2026-03-12: Deployed to canary pool (10 hosts) behind runway_orchestrator=true. Early telemetry shows stable p95 improvements and no OOMs in first 24h. Creating PR for review.
reviewers_feedback: Priya Shah: Good direction. Please add a safety cap on total GPU->CPU spill rate per-host to avoid saturating NIC and CPU memory. Also add an opt-out label for enterprise customers with strict data residency (ensure spills respect KMS/HSM boundaries).

Marcus Liu: Consider making soft compaction cancelable at sub-100ms granularity; we saw compaction run interference in a previous experiment. Also request more granular per-tenant metrics to debug noisy neighbors.
Leah Park: Request clarity on rollback cost (latency reversion) and add telemetry to estimate rollback impact before flipping flag to 50%.
